title: Cut a clean edit before lunch
goal: You will import footage, build and trim a two-minute edit, add transitions, and export an MP4 video.
prerequisites: Two or more video clips saved on your computer
A folder with enough space for the exported video

steps.action: Create a new Premiere Pro project named Two-Minute Edit.
steps.where: Premiere Pro Home screen, New Project button, Project name field, and Create button.
steps.why: The project stores your edit, media links, and export settings.
steps.checkpoint: The Premiere Pro editing workspace opens with Two-Minute Edit shown in the window title.
hint_levels: Start with the large button on the Home screen.
The New Project screen has a Project name field near the upper-left.
Click New Project, enter Two-Minute Edit in Project name, choose a project location, and click Create.

steps.action: Import the video clips you want to edit.
steps.where: File menu in the top menu bar, Import command, and the operating system file picker.
steps.why: Imported clips become available for arranging in your project.
steps.checkpoint: Thumbnail items for your video clips appear in the Project panel at the lower-left.
hint_levels: Look for the menu that handles files.
Import opens a file picker where you can select one or several clips.
Choose File > Import, select the clips with Ctrl-click, and click Open.

steps.action: Drag the imported clips into the empty Timeline panel in the order you want them to play.
steps.where: Project panel at the lower-left and Timeline panel across the lower-right.
steps.why: Placing the clips creates a sequence and forms the first rough edit.
steps.checkpoint: Colored clip blocks appear on the V1 and A1 tracks, and a sequence item appears in the Project panel.
hint_levels: Move the clip thumbnails toward the large empty panel at the bottom.
The Timeline uses horizontal tracks labelled V1 for video and A1 for audio.
In the Project panel, select the clips in playback order and drag them onto the empty Timeline panel.

steps.action: Cut each unwanted section at its beginning and end with the Razor tool.
steps.where: Tools panel beside the Timeline, Razor Tool button with the razor-blade icon, or keyboard shortcut C.
steps.why: These cuts isolate material that should not remain in the rough edit.
steps.checkpoint: Each unwanted section is separated from the surrounding footage by vertical edit lines.
hint_levels: Look beside the Timeline for the razor-blade icon.
Select the Razor Tool, then click the clip at both boundaries of an unwanted section.
Press C, click at the start and end of each unwanted section on the Timeline, then press V to return to the Selection Tool.

steps.action: Remove each isolated unwanted section with Ripple Delete.
steps.where: Timeline panel, right-click context menu on the isolated clip section, Ripple Delete command.
steps.why: Ripple Delete removes the section and automatically closes the resulting gap.
steps.checkpoint: The unwanted section disappears and the following clips move left with no empty space between them.
hint_levels: Use the command that deletes while closing the gap.
Right-click the isolated clip section and find Ripple Delete in its context menu.
With the Selection Tool active, right-click the unwanted section in the Timeline and click Ripple Delete.

steps.action: Drag clip edges to shorten the sequence until its duration is approximately two minutes.
steps.where: Timeline panel, left or right edge of each clip, with the Selection Tool active.
steps.why: Edge trimming refines cut timing without creating additional edits.
steps.checkpoint: The end of the final clip sits near 00:02:00:00 on the Timeline time ruler.
hint_levels: Adjust the boundaries between clips rather than cutting again.
Hover over a clip edge until the red trim-bracket cursor appears, then drag.
Press V, point at a clip edge in the Timeline, and drag left or right while watching the time ruler and Program Monitor.

steps.action: Add a Cross Dissolve transition to the cut where you want the clearest visual change.
steps.where: Effects panel, Video Transitions folder, Dissolve folder, and Cross Dissolve effect.
steps.why: A short dissolve can smooth a deliberate change between two adjacent shots.
steps.checkpoint: A transition block labelled Cross Dissolve straddles the selected cut in the Timeline.
hint_levels: Look in the panel that contains effects and transitions.
Expand Video Transitions and then Dissolve to find Cross Dissolve.
Choose Window > Effects if needed, expand Video Transitions > Dissolve, and drag Cross Dissolve onto the cut between two clips.

steps.action: Play the sequence from beginning to end and pause at any visible or audible problem.
steps.where: Program Monitor Play button above the Timeline, or Spacebar keyboard shortcut.
steps.why: A complete review catches gaps, abrupt cuts, and unwanted frames before export.
steps.checkpoint: The playhead reaches the end near 00:02:00:00 without showing black gaps or unintended footage.
hint_levels: Review what the viewer will actually receive.
Start at the sequence beginning and watch both picture and sound.
Press Home to move to the beginning, press Spacebar to play, and press Spacebar again whenever you need to stop.

steps.action: Open the Export workspace for the finished sequence.
steps.where: Export tab in the workspace bar at the top of Premiere Pro, or File > Export > Media.
steps.why: The Export workspace prepares the current sequence for an output file.
steps.checkpoint: The Export screen appears with Media File selected and a preview of your sequence visible.
hint_levels: Move from editing to the workspace used for output.
The Export tab is near the top of the Premiere Pro window.
Click Export at the top, or choose File > Export > Media.

steps.action: Export the sequence as an H.264 Match Source - Adaptive High Bitrate file.
steps.where: Export workspace, File Name, Location, Format, Preset, and Export controls.
steps.why: This creates a widely playable MP4 while preserving suitable source dimensions and frame rate.
steps.checkpoint: The export progress finishes and an .mp4 file appears in the selected folder.
hint_levels: Confirm the filename, destination, format, and preset before starting.
Use H.264 for Format and Match Source - Adaptive High Bitrate for Preset.
Set File Name and Location, choose Format > H.264, choose Preset > Match Source - Adaptive High Bitrate, and click Export.
